Requests use independent fresh monitors

boundaries: Each HTTP run creates a fresh monitor over one finite CSV upload. This does not add persistent browser sessions, incremental append, live observers, event/trace reader transform callbacks, or streaming-state checkpoint exchange; those public workflows remain in the review backlog.

The CSV adapter validates identifiers before invoking a monitor. Empty case/activity cells can fail import even though direct native receive operations skip invalid identifiers. Header/alias/trimming/quoting, multiline, dtype, ordering and large-file conventions remain independent gates.

The new input-order option reorders parser-assigned Event.input_order values, retaining parsed CSV arrival order across cases. Historical default HTTP/CLI order is case-grouped and timestamp-normalized. Eight current CLI comparisons prove ordinary importer-order shapes; input-order behavior is separately checked with controlled arrival-dependent native outputs.

Footprint constraints and temporal profile tuples use existing delimiter-based query adapters. Footprint activity names cannot contain commas or arrows; temporal names also exclude colons. Empty constraint text omits start/end checks, while explicit empty lists are rejected by the current route.

Footprint finalization removes open cases after native end checks. Token replay also removes finalized cases. Optional diagnostics retain the exact preceding prefix and per-case native termination outputs; top-level aggregate fields retain native conventions rather than being recomputed from displayed rows.

PNML streaming replay uses the existing single-source/sink workflow-net importer, not the general PNML document/marking API. Silent reachability remains bounded; no exhaustive-search or broader PNML marking/schema/arc parity is claimed.

Temporal conformance checks eligible earlier/later pairs on arrival. Missing or invalid timestamps can be skipped, and zero standard deviation can yield the native maximum finite distance. An absent explicit start field follows native attribute fallback conventions; no frontend timing recomputation is performed.

Native arrays retain their order. JSON object maps use JavaScript key enumeration in tables; numeric case IDs may display in a different order from native lexical object serialization. Full raw JSON remains byte-identical and termination arrays preserve native case order.

Existing response guards require safe integer counters. Request invisible bounds preserve the complete uint64 decimal range, but unbounded response counts, native-computation cancellation, browser cancellation races, persistent-state/concurrency and performance parity remain unproven.

Four assertion-enabled native suites pass with 167 hash-verified reused core objects. The first fresh optimized CLI build encountered an MSVC internal compiler error. A new immutable build uses /Od /Ob0 for freshly compiled executables; core algorithms are unchanged and no performance result is inferred.

The first export verifier assumed every DOM stylesheet was a local production asset and rejected the pre-existing external font stylesheet. The replacement independently verifies 35 CSV artifacts, 11 complete reports and two actual served local JS/CSS assets; external font rendering remains environment-dependent.
No reference implementation bodies or bytecode were inspected, no catalogue parity status was promoted, and the complete objective remains active.
